Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear note and the mark-up. I looped Marissa (Privacy) and Karthik (Product Security) in so we can confirm technical controls. High-level answers:

- Backup/DR carve-out: Redwood is willing to accept a limited backup retention carve-out for disaster recovery, but we typically limit retained backups to 60 days. Can you confirm whether Finbank needs the full 90 days, or whether 60 days with strong encryption and documented access controls would suffice?

- Transfers: Redwood uses the EU SCCs with the UK Addendum where applicable; we can provide a copy of the executed SCC annex. We also offer the option of acting as a Data Processor under customer-supplied SCCs if required.

- Subprocessors: we maintain a public subprocessors list and will provide the current snapshot. Redwood's process is to provide prior notice of material changes; for critical subprocessors we do permit review and escalation.

If Finbank needs 90 days for backups, Marissa, can you confirm whether we can accept 90 days with these mitigations: encryption-at-rest with customer KMS option, role-based access logs, and quarterly DR tests recorded for audit?

On Fri, 11 Sep 2026 at 08:34, kimberly_park@redwood.com wrote:
> If Finbank needs 90 days for backups, Marissa, can you confirm whether we can accept 90 days with these mitigations: encryption-at-rest with customer KMS option, role-based access logs, and quarterly DR tests recorded for audit?

Kimberly/Lisa —

We can accept a 90-day backup retention carve-out, provided the following are contractually bound and auditable:

1) Encryption: backups must be encrypted at rest using AES-256; customer-managed KMS where required, and keys segregated per customer.
2) Access controls: strict RBAC, multi-person approval for recovery operations, and immutable logs retained for at least 180 days.
3) Deletion semantics: when a customer issues a deletion request, we will remove primary/active copies within 30 days; backups may be retained up to 90 days but will be logically inaccessible (encrypted and not used for processing).
4) Disaster recovery testing: Redwood will provide a quarterly DR test report on request (redacted for other customers).
5) Subprocessors: current list is attached; Redwood will provide 30 days' prior notice for new subprocessors that may process EU data and will provide an escalation path for objections.

I'll attach a scoped DPA redline that adds a Backup/DR carve-out clause and the transfer mechanism language confirming SCCs + UK Addendum. 

Marissa Cole
Head of Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
